source: HAND-WRITTEN FIXTURE — not course data. Written by the harness slice so the runner is testable before the real utterance sets land at tools/tts-bakeoff/data/utterances-<lang>.json. The provenance blocks below are DELIBERATELY EMPTY: nothing here was pulled from course_seeds or course_practice_phrases and nothing here should be scored. Replace with the real generated set before any listening pass.

isolated_word.label: Isolated word
isolated_word.purpose: A single word with no carrier — the hardest case for a TTS that leans on sentence context. Most SSi LEGO debuts are exactly this.

short_phrase.label: Short phrase
short_phrase.purpose: BUILD-phrase length: a few LEGOs tiled together, often a fragment.

full_sentence.label: Full sentence
full_sentence.purpose: USE-phrase length: a complete natural sentence, the thing a learner hears most.

repeat_probe.label: Repeat probe
repeat_probe.purpose: One utterance rendered 20x with identical settings. Axis D and E live or die here: the sha256 spread across the 20 answers 'byte-identical across identical runs?' and the listening answers 'does the voice drift?'

utterances.difficulty_note: Fixture only. Word-initial 'dy' plus the 'u' vowel, which is the classic north/south split.
Fixture only. A fragment — no full stop, no closing intonation. Fragments are where TTS most often invents a sentence-final fall.

utterances.text: Dw i eisiau dysgu Cymraeg yn dda.

utterances.difficulty_note: Fixture only. THE 20x REPEAT TEST. Identical settings, twenty renders. Apostrophe elision plus a question contour.
